text:
emily: FYI got a pulse alert from gpu-telemetry: node gpu-node-22 showing burst of Xid errors + ECC corrected spikes. Wondering if we should wire up a healthhook that cordons nodes automatically when this happens.

rahul: +1 on a healthhook but we need to avoid noisy evictions. We saw earlier that transient XIDs during driver updates caused churn.

zara: Proposed rule: require either (a) >=3 Xid entries in a 5m sliding window OR (b) ECC_uncorrectable > 0 or corrected rate > 0.5% over 10m. If triggered, cordon + drain with a cooldown and rollback if metrics drop.

mike: Makes sense. Also: differentiate between k8s and Slurm flows. For k8s use cordon/drain; for Slurm mark node DOWN and requeue jobs. Sample commands: ``kubectl cordon gpu-node-22`` ``kubectl drain gpu-node-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`` ``scontrol update NodeName=gpu-node-22 State=DOWN Reason="gpu-healthhook: XID spikes"``

emily: Good call. We should also gate on whether the node is part of a Dedicated pool with reserved capacity; we can't just drain if it violates SLA. Add tenant-level policy: dev pools auto-evict, prod requires a manual ack or on-call override after alert.

rahul: Implementation notes: healthhook should be idempotent and do a compare-and-set to avoid racing with other operators. Pseudocode: ``if condition and not cordoned then set taint/cordon -> post ticket -> schedule eviction``. Keep an exponential backoff for rechecks to prevent flip-flopping.

zara: Also record the reason and metrics in node annotation so console/optimize can correlate: ``redwood.io/gpu-healthhook-reason`` and ``...-metrics-snapshot``. That helps for postmortems and auto-replace decisions.

mike: For noisy cases we can implement a "soft cordon" first: taint node with `gpu-probe-prohibited` which prevents new GPU pods but doesn't evict running pods. After 10m of persistence, escalate to hard drain. This reduces immediate capacity pain.

emily: Love soft cordon idea. For Slurm, maybe first set drain reason and set state DRAIN, then if counts persist escalate to DOWN and trigger node replace playbook.

rahul: Edge cases: 1) driver upgrade cycles that produce short XIDs -> ignore if rollout in progress (deploy-bot should create a suppress window). 2) multi-GPU nodes where only one card misbehaves -> we could leverage MIG-style isolation if available, but fallback to full node cordon otherwise.

zara: We should also add a safety net: if drain fails because of pod tolerations/daemonsets, healthhook should annotate and page on-call instead of stuck state. Include `--grace-period` and a max wait before aborting and paging.

emily: Can someone draft the k8s YAML for the healthhook controller + policy config? Keep policy data-driven so SRE/product can tweak thresholds without redeploy.

mike: I'll sketch a minimal policy example: ``policies: - name: xid-spike threshold: 3 window_m: 5 action: soft-cordon then hard-drain after_m: 10 cooldown_m: 30``

rahul: We also need telemetry signals beyond Xid/ECC: ECC corrected/unrecoverable, nvml_reset_count, thermal trips, and kernel oops related to GPU. Use a voting scheme so 2-of-3 signals triggers.

zara: For rollout, test in "dev-gpu" pool first, then a canary in staging with synthetic pup workloads. Add a metric for "healthhook-initiated-drain-rate" to monitor scope and false positives.

emily: Operational checklist: update on-call runbook, add runbook step for manual uncordon and how to replace card, add cost-provisioning note for capacity spikes.

mike: Also add an opt-out label for nodes we don't want auto-evicted (e.g., long-running debug nodes): ``redwood.io/auto-evict: "false"``

rahul: One more: ensure downstream autoscaler doesn't immediately spin up new nodes in the same AZ (we had a loop where autoscaler filled with new flaky nodes). Add a short zone-level cooloff or prefer healthy capacity from other AZs.

deploy-bot: Deploy plan created: "healthhook/v1 -> dev canary -> staging" (ETA 48h). CI job: `ci/healthhook-e2e`

ops-bot: Alert suppression created for driver-rollout windows when `deploy-bot` posts a rollout note.

emily: Thanks all. Action items: mike to PR policy schema, rahul to prototype controller logic with idempotency checks, zara to author test plan + runbook. I'll create the follow-up thread for prod policy (separate). :thumbsup:
